why: The versioned statement of WHAT IS EXPECTED, so that a percentage or a gate verdict can never be read without the manifest it was computed against. Written 16 September 2026 under the owner's engineering-control instruction; before it, 'fab-ready' was a judgement with no denominator, and every deliverable folder in the tree passed the final gate because verify_deliverable judges a folder against itself (appendix 32.201).

e5.title: PCB-E5 DOCK BLOCK
e5.note: a bare contact board: no schematic chain, no routed copper, built by build_e5.sh

promotion.why: Owner instruction of 16 September 2026: evidence produced before the rule registry exists is PRE_AUDIT and is not promoted. Running jobs are NOT stopped; their outputs are labelled and re-judged under the registry.
promotion.lifts_when: pcb_rules.yaml validates, rules_status.py computes a per-board result for every applicable rule, and the readiness gate state is READY_FOR_PROTOTYPE for the board being promoted.

evidence.why: Evidence written before this instant was taken under an unversioned rule set. It is readable as history and is INCONCLUSIVE for a current decision until it is reproduced under the registry fingerprint.

rule_set.fingerprint_note: null until the registry's first validated commit; rules_status.py refuses to compute a readiness state while it is null.

qualifier: WITH_WAIVERS is appended whenever any applicable rule on the board is WAIVED; it is never hidden by a percentage.

percentages.rule: verified_compliance_percent, waived_percent, failed_percent and inconclusive_percent share ONE denominator (applicable rule-board pairs required at the current phase) and sum to 100 subject to rounding; the project aggregate sums rule-board pairs and never averages board percentages.
